_comment: Provider entry commands for the framework dispatcher (dispatch.mjs). The framework owns scheduling; a provider is only a *callee* behind the task-interface ACL. Placeholders: {team} = the deployed team dir (~/.openclaw/team), {agent} = the dispatch agent argument, {repo} = the framework repo checkout ($OPENCLAW_TEAM_REPO, else .install-state.json.repoPath). The meerkat-taskpanel entries below resolve to scripts that now SHIP WITH THIS REPOSITORY (team/scripts/**, deployed by install.sh into {team}/scripts/**) — no longer a 'base runtime must pre-deploy them' assumption; entry-path coupling is resolved. The one exception is skillsUpdate: the skills pipeline (manifest.json + lock.json + fetch.mjs + update.mjs) is deliberately NOT deployed into {team}/ — it is a repo-side asset that install.sh drives in place ({repo}/skills/), and {team}/skills/ belongs to the task provider's ACL library. Provider dependency is now EXPLICIT (startup hard-fail, T-20261009-211234-providerdecouple): the entry scripts link the provider's ACL library at {team}/skills/task-ops/lib/ (installed by the task provider, intentionally not vendored) and, when it is absent, hard-fail with a clear 'provider 未安装' error + non-zero exit instead of a silent/cryptic no-op; dispatch.mjs still degrades to fire:false (never wakes a model) but its state.stderr carries that cause. checkAll now emits a {ok:true|false} envelope on its last line, so the dispatcher normalizes it (ok:false => fire:true, wakes only on failure) instead of classifying plain text as unparseable. skillsUpdate emits {fire,...} directly: fire:false when no upstream skill ref moved (zero-cost idle), fire:true with the change list when one did, and {ok:false,fire:true} on failure. The patrol entry now resolves to scripts/patrol.mjs — scanStale + an in-process 现态 re-check of the candidates BEFORE emit, so a candidate whose card has since reached done/in_review/blocked is dropped (reported in `dropped`) rather than fired; patrol-scan.mjs remains the single-source decision module it imports. This entry is what the live Gateway trigger should call; calling patrol-scan.mjs directly skips the pre-emit re-check. The dispatcher bounds the entry with OPENCLAW_TEAM_EVAL_TIMEOUT_MS (default 8000 ms) and the generated trigger passes exec({timeoutSeconds}); both stay under the Gateway's 30 s per-evaluation budget. Override per job with OPENCLAW_TEAM_POLL_CMD / OPENCLAW_TEAM_PATROL_CMD / OPENCLAW_TEAM_CHECKALL_CMD / OPENCLAW_TEAM_SKILLSUPDATE_CMD. Select a provider with OPENCLAW_TEAM_TASK_PROVIDER (default: meerkat-taskpanel). The provider key was renamed to `meerkat-taskpanel`; the pre-rebrand key `task-panel` still resolves, bidirectionally and with a one-line stderr note (legacy-name-compat — see LEGACY_PROVIDER_ALIAS in dispatch.mjs).
